title: Instrument model stage lifecycle and hardware cost tags
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds span tags for discrete model inference stages and hardware flavor tagging to enable stage-level latency and per-hardware cost attribution. New dashboard surfaces model-stage hot paths and a recommended alert tuning for stage p99s. Backwards compatible; no API changes.
description: Motivation: We currently have coarse request-level traces and a token-cost breakdown that doesn't attribute cost to specific inference stages or hardware flavors. This makes it hard to detect slow stages (tokenize/encode/kv-lookup/attention/decode) and to correlate expensive tails with particular GPU classes. This PR: (1) tags spans with a normalized model_stage field (tokenize, embed, kv_fetch, attention, decode, postprocess) and a hardware_flavor tag (e.g. A100-v4, H100-80GB, T4). (2) emits a compact per-stage cost estimate derived from per-device per-token ms * device-cost-rate to allow downstream aggregation without exploding cardinality. (3) introduces sampling rules to upsample rare long-decode traces while keeping overall span volume bounded. (4) ships a Grafana dashboard and JSONnet panels for model-stage latency heatmap, hardware cost splits, and stage-level p99s by model and region. Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-8872/model-stage-telemetry (internal). Checklist: - [x] Add model_stage span tagging in runtime (serve/tracing) - [x] Add hardware_flavor tag from node metadata - [x] Cost attribution helper and exporter for metrics pipeline - [x] Adaptive sampling policy (stage-aware) - [x] Dashboard panels + docs - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Updated changelog and release notes Backwards compatibility: tagging is additive and metric names are new. No customer-facing API changes.

discussion: Marco Nguyen (reviewer): Nice end-to-end. Two questions: 1) How do we avoid cardinality explosion if models have dynamic model_id tags? 2) Is the cost heuristic safe to use with autoscaling (because cost-rate varies by region)?

Aisha Patel (author): For (1) we normalize model_id to model_name and strip large hashed tags in span-level tags. The sampling and downstream rollups are by model_name not full model_revision. For (2) the exporter attaches node_region and hardware_flavor; the heuristic multiplies per-device ms by device-rate taken from a region-config map. We'll document caveats in telemetry/model-stage.md.
Ellen Park (reviewer): Can the adaptive sampler cause us to miss KV fetch regressions which are often short but frequent?

Aisha Patel: Good point. Sampler is stage-aware: KV_FETCH keeps baseline sampling at 10% and an additional rule increases sampling for KV spans whose latency spikes above a low threshold. Added tests to validate this behavior.
Gustavo Rios (approver): Approved after nits. Please add a note in observability runbook about alert thresholds and example queries.
